title: Mr. Winkle's Wobbly Plan
markdown:
The annual Sunflower Market in Bramblebrook buzzed with happy noise. Sweet fruit and fresh roots perfumed the air. Oranges rolled like tiny suns. Cheerful chatter promised a day of fun. But at the heart of it all, no one was more ready than Mr. Winkle.

Mr. Reginald Winkle was Bramblebrook’s very tidy lizard librarian. His green scales shone. His eyes, magnified by spectacles, sparkled. He believed any job, no matter how small, became art with a good diagram. Sorting old scrolls was best with careful plans on paper.

“Rosa, my friend,” Mr. Winkle announced. He unfurled a scroll as big as a picnic blanket. Rosa, his mole friend, blinked up at him. Rosa knew the earth’s secrets and always saw the practical side.

“Today,” he said, tail twitching, “we won’t just have a market. We’ll make it perfectly organised. We’ll make market stalls the best they can be. Look.” He pointed to the scroll. “The Optimal Produce Arrangement System.”

Rosa shuffled closer. The drawing was amazing. Straight lines, arrows, coloured squares — all perfect. “Well, Reginald,” she rumbled. “It’s very neat.”

“Neat and logical.” He beamed. He tapped a square. “See how the Citrus Cove flows into the Berry Biosphere? No awkward changes. And the Earth’s Embrace roots are placed to stop moisture from reaching the fruit. Very scientific.” He was so lost in his plan he didn’t see the curious crowd gathering.

“I never thought about my turnips getting damp,” said Mrs. Higgins, who had rosy apples and a rosy smile. “It makes sense.”

But just as Mr. Winkle was about to talk about cheese, a small hand tugged his elbow. He looked down. Lily, a girl with bright eyes like blueberries and freckles like a constellation, stood there.

“Excuse me, Mr. Winkle? Where do the Sunshine Surprise berries go on your diagram?”

He froze. He looked at his scroll. Citrus Cove, Berry Biosphere, Root Realm. But there was no place for Sunshine Surprise berries. They were new. Odd fruits, all different sizes, glowing yellow.

“Ah, yes,” he stammered. His perfect composure wobbled. “The Sunshine Surprise berries aren’t in the main plan. My apologies.”

Lily tilted her head. “But they’re the best part. And they don’t fit in the Berry Biosphere if they’re all wobbly and different sizes.”

The market chatter stopped. The Sunshine Surprise berries, with their wobbly shapes, were pure joy and surprise. The logical plan had missed something important.

Mr. Winkle’s green scales seemed to dim. His grand plan had a wobble. Therefore Rosa, practical and kind, nudged him. “Perhaps,” she rumbled softly, “they belong somewhere special, Reginald. Where everyone can see their surprise. A spot for unexpected delights, wobbly or not?”

A spark lit his eyes. Rosa was right. He looked at Lily’s earnest face. A new idea, less about perfection and more about charm, began to grow. “A special spot,” he repeated, voice stronger. “Yes.”

Therefore, with Rosa guiding him, Mr. Winkle and some helpers quickly changed their plan. They forgot the straight lines. They made a small hill of soft straw right at the market entrance. On it they placed the Sunshine Surprise berries. They glowed in the sun, like fallen stars. Their wobbly shapes looked cheerfully uneven. It wasn’t neat. It wasn’t in the diagram. But it was wonderfully cheerful.

When the market opened, everyone stopped at the Sunshine Surprise berries. Children giggled. Adults smiled. Even the grumpiest shopkeeper cracked a grin.

Mr. Winkle watched, spectacles shining. His plan hadn’t been perfect. There were delightful surprises and a bit of chaos. He saw Lily happily picking berries, her face full of joy. He looked at his rolled-up diagram, then at the lively market. The berries, in all their wobbly glory, sat where no square had been drawn, and the oranges, which had rolled like tiny suns, kept rolling, unbothered, into a corner the Optimal Produce Arrangement System had never named.
characters: Mr. Winkle (a tidy lizard librarian), Rosa (the mole friend)
audience: children aged 11-12, amusing story for older children
